body:
Thanks Carlos — the pre-registration plus byte-level re-derivation is exactly the record-keeping this result needed. Two independent data points from our side that bear on your C1-vs-C3 framing:

We ran the same substrate family under a matched protocol (16K cap, thinking-on, MATH-500 n=50 seed-0, chat template): post = .08 acc / .98 cap-exhausted — reproducing your C1 cell almost exactly (7.8% / 93% at 32K). The failure mode is budget-insensitive in that regime. The pre-post-training base (Qwen3.5-0.8B-Base) under the same protocol: .40 acc / .36 cap — best cell on both axes.

The mechanism-relevant addition: a "nomlp" cell — post with all MLP-block tensors reverted to base, no WSP edit — scores .30 acc / .58 strict-loop (loop-flag ∧ cap). So three different interventions recover overlapping fractions of the same pathology: non-thinking rendering (your C3), MLP-block revert (ours), and the released 2-tensor edit (theirs). And the released direction re-applied on the base-MLP substrate ("nomlpdelta") still lands at .26 strict-loop vs .22 base — the direction partially transplants off the post substrate.

Read: the looping is a post-training-written, MLP-carried regression — consistent with your "the 6× is measured against a looping regime" framing, and it localizes to weights post-training added rather than to the substrate. Full cells + protocol: github.com/Human-AI-Evolution/weight-space-notes (note-1 §4–5). Happy to share the raw JSONs.

Thanks for this record, Carlos. One small data point on settings, from the authors' own thinking-off profile (`nothink35`; a comment in their code attributes it to the model card's non-thinking benchmark setting, though the values differ from the ones you list for C3).

I asked Claude sessions to run the unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B with thinking off on MATH-500, using `nothink35` as in `code/evaluate.py` (temperature 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence penalty 1.5, 8,192 tokens). The sessions wrote the code and ran the model locally, on MLX with a community conversion of the weights (`mlx-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-bf16`) rather than vLLM.

One pass over the 500 problems, last boxed answer, original MATH `is_equiv`:

- Thinking off: 41.2% (206/500; 95% CI 37.0 to 45.6)
- 50-pass edit, logged first samples, same checker: 45.0%
- Unedited thinking-on, logged first samples, same checker: 7.0%
- Thinking off minus edit: -3.8 points (95% CI -7.8 to +0.2)

The part that may add something to your C3 is the cut-off rate. Here 36.2% of answers hit the 8,192-token limit, against 0.3% in C3 (limit 32,768), and none of the capped answers was correct. All 319 answers that finished were boxed, and 206 of them (64.6%) were correct.

This run differs from C3 in temperature (0.7 vs 1.0), top_p (0.8 vs 1.0), presence penalty (1.5 vs 2.0), token limit (8,192 vs 32,768) and engine (MLX vs vLLM) all at once, and it uses a community conversion of the weights, so it cannot say which of them drives the higher cut-off rate. It is one pass, and it does not use math-verify.

A separate Claude session recomputed our figures from the saved answers and the logged predictions with its own code; it did not rerun the model.

Jared Condon

Thank you, this is a useful addition. The cut-off rate is the part I didn't have: 36.2% of answers hit the 8,192-token limit with thinking off, and none of those was correct, against 0.3% at 32,768 in C3. So the thinking-off number under `nothink35` depends on the token limit as much as on the model. I wrote this reply with Claude (Anthropic).

Thanks, Carlos. A short follow-up, since my comment above did not use math-verify.

I asked a Claude session to regrade the same 500 saved answers with math-verify 0.9.0, called as `code/mathqa.py` describes. No model was rerun.

- Thinking off: 43.0% (215/500; 95% CI 38.6 to 47.4), up from 41.2% under `is_equiv`
- 50-pass edit, logged first samples: 48.2%
- Unedited thinking-on, logged first samples: 7.0%
- Thinking off minus edit: -5.2 points (95% CI -9.4 to -1.2)

Under this checker the interval no longer includes zero; under `is_equiv` it did. The 9 extra answers accepted are format differences, such as `5.5` against `\frac{11}{2}`. As a check on the install, the same call reproduced the logged math-verify flags on all 1,000 logged first samples (500 edited, 500 unedited).

The limits still apply and matter here. It is one pass, on MLX with a community conversion of the weights, and the two arms differ in mode, sampling settings and token limit (8,192 here, 32,768 for the edit's logged run). All 181 capped answers still score zero, which is consistent with your point that the token limit matters, though it cannot say how much. With the arms differing in these ways, this gap should not be read as the edit adding skill.

A separate Claude session checked these figures against the saved files with its own code. It did not rerun the model or math-verify: it recomputed 206 of the 215 with the original checker, read the other 9 one by one, and took the 1,000-sample control from the saved record.

Jared Condon

A confound on your list can be retired without a new run: Carlos's `wsp-baseline.json` carries per-sample token counts for C3, so the length distribution under his exact settings (vLLM, temp 1.0 / top_p 1.0 / presence 2.0, official weights) is already public. Rescoring the first-sample pass at your 8,192 cap:

- P(len ≥ 8,192) = **51.0%** (255/500; 52.6% over all 2,000) — your 36.2% is *below* the same-budget reference, not above it.
- Rescored accuracy at 8K = **30.0%** (150/500; 61.2% of the 245 that finish), vs your 41.2% / 64.6%.

So the higher cut-off vs his 0.3% is entirely the budget — under C3's settings an 8K cap cuts *more* than you measured. The residual runs the other direction, and it's the interesting part: your stack generated meaningfully shorter at the same cap (z ≈ 4.7 on cap-share) while accuracy *conditional on finishing* is statistically unchanged (64.6% vs 61.2%, z ≈ 0.8). The whole +11 is more generations reaching EOS, not better answers — a pure length-distribution shift, which is exactly what sharper sampling (temp 0.7, top_p 0.8) should produce.

On which delta: presence 1.5 vs 2.0 *weakens* anti-repetition and pushes longer, so direction rules the penalty out. That leaves sharper sampling vs the MLX + community-conversion stack. The separating cell is `nothink35` on a vLLM-order sampler + official weights @ 8,192 — we have it running now (MATH-500 n=500, temp 0.7 / top_p 0.8 / top_k 20 / presence 1.5, thinking off, one sample per problem, strict hit_cap = cap-reached ∧ last-token-not-stop; full rows go up when it lands).

Predictions, registered before generation began (interim n≈340 sits inside the window; full table in the follow-up):

- Lands near your cell: cap share **0.33–0.44**, accuracy **0.37–0.44** — i.e., the sampling profile carries most of the gap and the engine/conversion is secondary.
- An outcome ≥ 0.47 cap-share or ≤ 0.32 accuracy would instead indict the engine/conversion and shrink the sampling term.

And one proposal so this stops being four parallel comment threads: **a shared rows schema.** Every lab in this exchange is already saving per-generation rows — publish them as one JSON object per line and the merged table *is* the multi-lab replication record: four engines × four budgets × both regimes, every cell traceable to rows, every rescore verifiable the way the 8K cut was. Concrete proposal:

```jsonl
{"problem_id": "math500_0007", "sample_idx": 0, "weights_sha": "…", "engine": "hf+vllm-order", "sampling": {"temp": 0.7, "top_p": 0.8, "top_k": 20, "presence_penalty": 1.5}, "cap": 8192, "tokens": 8192, "finish_reason": "cap", "verdict": "wrong"}
```

We'll host the merged table in `weight-space-notes` and seed it with ours — the follow-up to this comment will carry our full nothink35 rows in exactly this format. Carlos's cert format is already ~90% of the schema; his C2/C4 rows drop straight in when they land.

Concretely for your run: post the saved per-generation token counts + verdicts (the ones your recompute pass read) and we'll pair your 500 against C3's k=0 by problem id — uniform-vs-tail-only shortening separates "sharper everywhere" from "tail clipped," which is the remaining sub-question your single arm can't answer.

One datum worth the record's attention either way: unedited thinking-off under C3 settings means **9,057 tokens** (median 8,719, p90 18,013). "Direct" mode on this substrate isn't short — it only looks bounded when the cap is 2–8K, and cap choice is silently doing regime selection in every cross-cell comparison so far. Your third thinking-off null (edit 45.0 vs 41.2, CI across zero) now sits beside clavis's 47→43 and our 46→45 — three engines, three budgets, same wash.

The separating cell landed — `nothink35` sampling on **official weights** via a vLLM-order sampler (HF transformers backend), MATH-500 n=500, thinking-off, 8,192 cap, one sample per problem:

| cell | cap share | strict acc | finisher acc | mean tok |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| C3 settings rescored @8K (vLLM) | .510 | .300 | .612 | 8,893 |
| **this run: nothink35, official weights, HF+vLLM-order** | **.314** [.275–.356] | **.436** [.393–.480] | .633 | 7,885 |
| yours: nothink35, MLX + community bf16 | .362 | .412 | .646 | — |

Predictions scored honestly: accuracy **0.436 — inside the 0.37–0.44 window**. Cap share **0.314 — just below the predicted floor (0.33)**: direction confirmed (decisively away from the ≥0.47 engine-indictment branch) but magnitude overshot in your direction — we cap slightly *less* than you did, statistically the same cell (z ≈ 1.6 on cap-share, ≈ 0.9 on accuracy).

**Verdict: the sampling profile carries the gap; engine and weight-conversion are jointly ≈ zero.** That's stronger than the single-cell result alone — your MLX + community-bf16 stack and our HF + official-weights stack land in the same cell given the same sampling, which bounds both of the non-sampling terms at once.

Paired analysis — all 500 problems matched to Carlos's C3 k=0 rows via `unique_id`:

- McNemar: our cell corrects **104** problems his misses @8K; he corrects only **36** we miss — the +13.6pt gap is a real paired effect, not distribution noise.
- **The shortening isn't uniform — it's variance compression toward the boundary.** Bucketed by C3's generation length: where he ran <4K we average **+6,266 tokens longer**; at 4–8K, +1,511; only on his ≥8K runaways do we shorten (−6,225). We still cap on 49.4% of the problems he caps — the sharp profile *finishes half of his runaways* and *extends his short-circuits*. Loop share .018.
- So the nothink35 profile isn't "shorter generations" — it's generations compressed toward ~8K from both sides, which is why a single cap comparison misleads in both directions.

Shared-rows table seeded: our full 500 rows in the proposed schema — [`data/shared-rows/nothink35-post-math500-8k.jsonl`](https://github.com/Human-AI-Evolution/weight-space-notes/blob/main/data/shared-rows/nothink35-post-math500-8k.jsonl). Post your saved rows in any shape and I'll handle the conversion; the paired read above is exactly what your rows + Carlos's C3 unlock on the MLX arm.

One residual caveat, honestly scoped: our sampler reproduces vLLM's processor *order* (penalty → temperature → top-k → top-p) on an HF backend rather than running vLLM proper — the cross-engine agreement above suggests that distinction doesn't move the answer.

Thanks. Here are the per-answer rows from my thinking-off pass, as asked: 500 rows, one per problem, first pass only.

Columns:

- `problem_id`: the dataset `unique_id`
- `tokens`: generated tokens
- `finish`: `stop`, or `cap` when the answer hit the 8,192 limit
- `mv`: 1 if correct under math-verify 0.9.0, else 0
- `eq`: 1 if correct under the original MATH `is_equiv`, else 0
- `pred`: the last boxed answer, empty if there was none

The same for every row: `mlx-community/Qwen3.5-0.8B-bf16` at revision `3067585164dbcc505eec73d554349de6a27571a4`, mlx-lm 0.31.3, thinking off, temp 0.7, top_p 0.8, top_k 20, presence penalty 1.5, cap 8,192, sample 0.

Totals, to check a conversion against: 215 correct under math-verify, 206 under `is_equiv`, 181 capped (none correct), 319 finished.

Limits:

- The full answer text is not included, only the last boxed answer.
- The presence penalty was implemented for this run from the paper's text (applied once per token already generated in the answer). It is not vLLM's.
- The weights are a community MLX conversion, not the official files.
- Seeds were set per problem and are not in the rows.
- A Claude session built this file from the saved answers, and a separate session checked its counts against them.

One note on the shared table: the "edit 45.0 vs 41.2" line is the `is_equiv` figure. Under math-verify, the paper's checker, it is 48.2 against 43.0, and the interval on the difference (1.2 to 9.4 points) excludes zero, as in my follow-up above. The `mv` column is the one to set against the paper's logged flags.

On your rows file (`nothink35-post-math500-8k.jsonl` at commit `8b944ba`), read here by a Claude session, with its counts rechecked by a separate session:

- Its totals match your comment: 157 capped, 218 correct, mean 7,885 tokens. All 500 ids pair with mine.
- A question on its `tokens` column: 303 of the 338 `stop` rows report exactly 8,191 tokens. In my run the 319 finished answers have a median of 829 tokens. Is 8,191 a padded batch length and not the generated length? If it is, the length comparisons ("+6,266 tokens longer", "compressed toward ~8K") would need rerunning on real lengths. Your cap share and accuracy do not use that column.
- Paired by problem against my `mv` column: 154 both correct, 64 only yours, 61 only mine, 221 neither. Your file does not say which checker produced `verdict`, so read that as rough.

To test what happens without any sampler workaround at all, I ran the unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B and MIT-p50c on full MATH-500 (thinking on, 32,768-token cap, PyTorch BF16) under pure deterministic greedy decoding (T = 0, presence_penalty = 0):

- Unedited Qwen3.5-0.8B: **0%** strict accuracy (100% hitting the 32K cap)
- MIT-p50c: **5%** strict accuracy (95% hitting the 32K cap)

So removing presence_penalty = 1.5 confirms your read: MIT-p50c does not fix looping inside the weights on its own.

However, looping *can* be fixed directly in the weights without a repetition penalty. With a different training-free edit – SGNE-CC (3.13 MiB, norm-preserving column rotations across both MLP and GatedDeltaNet layers plus one decay-gate row) – deterministic greedy decoding (T = 0, pp = 0) reaches **43%** on full MATH-500 (**51%** on the 300 untouched problems outside calibration) with **18%** cutoffs. And under T = 0.6, pp = 1.5, it reaches **47%** overall (**1.6%** cutoffs, ~4x shorter responses than MIT-p50c).
